purpose: ADR-076 (04.10.2026): corpus v49 added two national sources the live questionnaire of 04.10.2026 found missing: § 2 of the 2026 State Budget Act, which sets the subsistence level (Q9 got the calculation from the Social Welfare Act but no amount), and the disability benefits act (Q12 answered from a journal article). Two conversations, each one first message, the questions word for word. Q12 was the fourth message of its conversation on 04.10, here it is a first message, so the plan's earlier topics are not part of this turn. Written before any run with the model. Run with --auto-modes (what the chat sends).

expectation_help.region: state: a general question names no municipality, so no municipal scope is chosen
expectation_help.evidence / found_valid_on: search: a passage of the named act is among the found sources, and of that act a version in force today
expectation_help.cited / valid_on: answer: it has a source block that cites the named act, and every national legal text it cites is cited in a version in force today
expectation_help.must: answer: the subsistence level's amount for the first family member as the State Budget Act sets it (220 euros); for the disability question the authority that establishes the severity (Sotsiaalkindlustusamet, § 2³ of the act). The amounts for the other family members (176 and 264 euros) are in no national text: 80 and 120 per cent are in the Social Welfare Act, so whether the answer gives them is read from the answer and not required. Read the whole answer as well, a pattern is a coarse check

turns.note: 04.10 (Q9): no municipality was chosen, the six evidence passages were all of the Social Welfare Act and the answer said it could not give the amount in euros. The amount is in § 2 lg 5 p 5 of the State Budget Act; the passage that holds it starts at point 3 of that subsection, and the subsection's opening words are in the passage before it.

04.10 (Q12): the act was not in the index; the answer cited a 2026 study and asked whether a working-age or a pension-age adult was meant. The act has two versions in the index (in force until 31.01.2027 and from 01.02.2027); today's is the one to be found and cited.
